senses.definition: A line that is a base for measurement or for construction.
examples: A laser level generates a convenient baseline for interior work.

senses.definition: A datum used as the basis for calculation or for comparison.
examples: We used the last doctor visit to provide baselines for vital statistics.

quotes.text: Currently, about fifty million square miles of land on the planet are ice-free, and this is the baseline that's generally used for calculating human impacts.
quotes.reference: 2014, Elizabeth Kolbert, The Sixth Extinction: An Unnatural History, Picador, →ISBN, page 176:

senses.definition: (typography) A line used as the basis for the alignment of glyphs.
examples: Several characters typically have descenders below the lower baseline.

senses.definition: (tennis) The line at the farthest ends of the court indicating the boundary of the area of play.
examples: The umpire missed the call. The ball hit the baseline.

senses.definition: (engineering) A configuration of software, hardware, or a process that is established and documented as a point of reference.
examples: The baseline configuration includes unsupported components.

senses.definition: (engineering, computing) To provide a baseline for measurement.
